title: Rational coordinate comodules over a commutative ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ a commutative Hopf $R$-algebra. For an affine $R$-group scheme $G$ use its canonical coordinate Hopf algebra $R[G]$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra], with its actual structure map and group law. A rational module on an $R$-module $M$ is an $R$-linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_R C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] satisfying $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, with the canonical tensor unit and associativity identifications. The invariant endomorphism submodule is the kernel of the $R$-linear map $T\mapsto\rho\circ T-(T\otimes1)\circ\rho$ on $\operatorname{End}_R(M)$; these are precisely the invariants for conjugation. Define the coefficient evaluation map $(\operatorname{End}_R(M)\otimes_R C)\to\operatorname{End}_R(M\otimes_R C)$ by $(T\otimes c)(m\otimes d)=T(m)\otimes cd$, extended linearly. These definitions impose no field, finiteness or nonzero hypothesis on $R,C,M$.
